title: T1055.013 — Process Injection - Process Doppelgänging
subtitle: Interactive walkthrough of Process Injection - Process Doppelgänging with the technique-specific attack path and defender evidence.
aria: Animated diagram of Process Doppelgänging. An attacker sends a loader to a Windows victim host. The loader opens an NTFS transaction, writes a malicious program file into it, asks the kernel to map it as an image section in memory, rolls the transaction back so the file vanishes, and starts the payload process from the memory section. A SOC evidence feed on the right fills in step by step, ending with behavioral detection, host isolation, and memory capture.

steps.title: Delivery
steps.caption: The attacker sends a malspam email with a link. The user downloads the loader. The loader is a normal file on disk at this point.
steps.defender: a file-creation alert for a new executable in a user folder is the first and only file artifact.

steps.title: Transaction opens
steps.caption: The loader calls NtCreateTransaction and gets a handle to a transacted file. Windows holds every write to this file in a pending state.
steps.defender: almost no telemetry exists for this step in default logging.

steps.title: Malicious PE is written
steps.caption: The loader writes the payload PE (portable executable) into the transacted file. The bytes exist only inside the pending transaction.
steps.defender: antivirus file scans and FIM (file integrity monitoring) see nothing, because no persisted file appears.

steps.title: Image section is created
steps.caption: The loader calls NtCreateSection with the SEC_IMAGE flag on the transacted file. The kernel maps it as a program image in memory.
steps.defender: coverage is sparse; some EDR kernel sensors or ETW (Event Tracing for Windows) providers may log an image load from a temporary path.

steps.title: Rollback
steps.caption: The loader calls NtRollbackTransaction. The transacted file vanishes from the file system. The in-memory section stays valid.
steps.defender: file monitors report no deletion, because the file never persisted. This is the core evasion trick.

steps.title: Process and thread start
steps.caption: The loader calls NtCreateProcessEx with the section and then NtCreateThreadEx at the entry point. The malicious image runs as a process with no file behind it.
steps.defender: the EDR flags a process whose reported image path no longer resolves on disk. This is the strongest native signal.

steps.title: Payload stage runs
steps.caption: The payload executes its task. In the 2018 FIN7 reporting the payload was SynAck ransomware; here it behaves like an implant or ransomware stage.
steps.defender: a behavioral detection fires on the malicious actions, not on a file.

steps.title: Defender response
steps.caption: The SOC isolates the host, captures memory, and scans for orphaned image sections. Behavioral evidence, not file evidence, drives the case.
steps.defender: containment works even when the disk holds no payload, because the process is still alive in memory.
